title: It signifies liberation
text: “That was rude of me. Itsuki-dono, then—I hereby declare a duel between Itsuki-dono, the Bow Hero, and the Shield Hero!”

After offering a token apology, Trash declared the duel between Father and Itsuki. I watched the proceedings in silence, I say. After all, I was busy administering some educational guidance to Rabbit Guy. Getting rather tired of the whole affair, I decided to hand off the now-twitching Rabbit Guy to Crocodile Guy.
“Whoa, Theo… I thought you were being quiet, but this is what was going on?”
“But… I suppose. It seems we have no choice but to bear witness to Shield Hero-sama’s valiant form. Spear Hero… would you kindly go a bit easier on him?”

He let out some kind of sigh, but I paid it no mind. And so we moved to the castle courtyard for the duel. Seeing Rabbit Guy convulsing, Father looked briefly startled at first—but then it was time for strategy talk.
“Well, there was a lot of commotion, but hey, we managed to get things to a duel after all.”
“Are you quite alright? I stayed silent, but I would have gladly stepped in and caused a ruckus, indeed.”

There was, after all, the option of charging in alongside Crocodile Guy, tormenting the Crimson Swine, beating Trash black and blue, rescuing Éclair, and making our escape from the castle. And the castle would become a sea of flame. HAHAHA.
But Father surely had his reasons for doing things this way. So this Motoyasu shall steel his heart and watch the duel unfold.
“No, no, I’m glad you kept quiet. As for how to deal with Theo—well, Theo does get weirdly worked up whenever Itsuki’s the one he’s dealing with, so it couldn’t be helped… sorry about that.”
Once Father apologized, the paralyzed Rabbit Guy settled down. Incidentally, he was being carried princess-style by Crocodile Guy.
“Do you have some kind of winning strategy for this duel, I wonder? If things look like they’re going your way, those two are bound to pull something underhanded, are they not?”
Weaken Itsuki with poison, then pin him down—only for the Crimson Swine to interfere—and once that’s weathered, Trash launches a furious assault? Something like that?

“Yeah. Don’t worry, if you know how the other side’s going to act, you can prepare a counter for just about anything. Well, Motoyasu-kun, all you need to do is keep watch so Shion, Theo, and Yuki-chan and the others don’t jump in.”
“Understood! Should any of them so much as think of moving, I shall put them down by any means necessary, indeed.”
“Right now… put down. He said. This, person.”
Oh my, it seemed the paralysis on Rabbit Guy had worn off. Shall I administer an additional dose of Silence Lance? I made the tip of my spear glint menacingly.
“He’ll behave, so please stop…”
Since Crocodile Guy asked so nicely, I decided to hold off. But should he make any foolish moves, I would silence him at once.
“W-well… just take it easy. Shion, it’s fine, don’t worry.”
“…Liberacion.”
“Eh?”

“My true name is Liberacion. According to what I heard from my father and Seaetto, it means liberation. I was named with the hope of being freed from the clan’s decree of faith and loyalty toward the Shield Hero.”
Crocodile Guy went on to say that it was a bitter irony of fate that he, of all people, should end up devoting his loyalty to the Shield Hero.
“Great Shield Hero-sama, I shall become your weapon and your strength. I only pray that you will grant me a battle I am capable of enduring.”
“Ah, well, everyone worries too much. Don’t worry. Just watch.”
With that, Father finished his conversation with Crocodile Guy and began walking toward Itsuki.
“What a troublesome commotion this has all turned into,” Yuki-chan remarked. She, like me, had been silently watching the proceedings. Indeed, quite so.
“Boo… this is no fun—Kou wants to go home already.”
“Kou, if you tell the children back in the village about all this, I’m sure they’ll listen with great excitement.”
“Eh? Really—? But Kou doesn’t know if he can tell it in a fun way—Kou will ask Elmelo to teach him.”
Yuki-chan and Kou were having quite the heartwarming little exchange, I say.
“Well then… shall we begin?”

Now then, the duel was about to start. Incidentally, Father had managed to learn magic as well—just in time, I say. Apparently, thanks to studying together with Rabbit Guy, he’d managed to pick it up. Which meant that, compared to the looped Father who’d stayed behind in Melromarc, this one now had considerably more cards up his sleeve.

The scene unfolding before me bore a striking resemblance to the duel between Father and Itsuki that lived on in my memory. This present Father, having heard my account of things, seemed to have even greater odds in his favor now, and yet I couldn’t help but feel my heart pound with nerves. With what sort of strategy would Father liven up this farce that was practically a public execution? It would be quite rude of me to feel both this much unease and this much excitement at the same time, wouldn’t it? For now, Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy remained uncaptured, merely watching alongside me.

“Now then, let the duel between the Bow Hero and the Shield Hero begin! Victory shall be determined either by driving the opponent to the very brink of a finishing blow, or by their admission of defeat!”

Just as before, Father was readying his stance in preparation. So was his strategy still to counter Itsuki with poison and let it run its course until he collapsed? Even now, I felt the overwhelming urge to leap in and lend my strength, again and again. I could have done so if I wished—but that wasn’t the outcome Father wanted… such is the way of things, most inconvenient indeed. If it got out that Father was fighting here for Éclair’s sake, it would surely be horribly misunderstood. As for Éclair herself, I rather thought that if we simply told her the truth and let her out of her cell, she’d come out on her own accord anyway. She did seem to want to see the Queen, after all—so really, all we had to do was ship her out.
“Fighting against Naofumi-san, a weak class, the outcome is already decided, but this is for justice’s sake. You’d best admit defeat sooner rather than later.”

“Let me teach you something, Itsuki. In most online games, what they call a tank class is actually pretty strong in PvP. I’m going to pound the terrifying truth of a shield that can’t attack right into your skull.”
Father’s provocation, I say. He was about to pound reality into Itsuki, who blindly worshipped his game knowledge.
“More than anything, Itsuki, I think it’s about time you realized something.”
“……I won’t listen to someone who’s done whatever he pleased and never faced any punishment for it!”

“I’ll apologize for putting you in a position where you couldn’t back down. Well… you’re probably going to have another unpleasant experience, but think of it as the price for drowning in your own sense of justice.”

Itsuki kicked away Father’s mercy. Even Father, patient as he was, answered as though the time for leniency had passed. There was no doubt this Itsuki needed a good scolding. Even the Itsuki from my memories, who knew the truth, raised no objection—unanimous agreement, in fact. And yet, for some reason, Father kept warning me not to do anything unnecessary. By “unnecessary,” did he perhaps mean shrinking my spear down to toothpick size and firing off an Air Strike Javelin or something? I supposed I could just as easily blast it straight into Itsuki’s head the very instant the Crimson Swine cast her spell. He’d be knocked out cold in an instant. But since Father clearly had some plan in mind, I decided to keep quiet and watch. If anything, my true mission was to keep watch over Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy, in case either of them lost their patience and did something unnecessary themselves.
“Now then—begin!”
The moment the announcer gave the signal to start, Father and Itsuki both moved.
“Uoooooooooooooooooh!”
“Haaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
Just as before, Itsuki took a step back, drew his bow taut, and loosed an arrow at Father as he charged forward. Naturally, Father caught the arrow and stopped it.
“What!?”
If he thought that would be enough to stop Father, he was sorely mistaken. Just as I remembered, Itsuki kept his distance and immediately fired off several more arrows in succession.
“Your aim is accurate, but that’s all it is.”

Without even using Air Strike Shield, Father deflected the arrows with his shield alone, charging straight toward Itsuki in a single line. Well now! To think his skill had risen to the point where he could parry Itsuki’s attacks without relying on skills at all—how astonishing. But then again, this Father had been training all this while through his time spent with the slaves, so perhaps it was only natural that he could pull this off. He had, after all, moved around quite nimbly while playing with Wolf. What’s more, he’d participated to some degree in training sessions with Panda and the old woman as well.
